headline: Evergreen Consultants increasing cash allocations as an underappreciated uncorrelated asset in an uncertain environment
reasoning: Angela Ashton argues that cash is a highly valuable but often overlooked uncorrelated asset, particularly because its behaviour in a market downturn is well understood and predictable. Evergreen has been building cash weightings across portfolios as part of a broader defensive tilt. She draws a parallel to Berkshire Hathaway's record cash pile as validation of this approach.
quote: What we are doing is we're increasing cash slightly, um, where we can. And for me, cash is a great uncorrelated asset that most people overlook. Um, you know, we know how it's going to behave if things fall. You know, turn to custard. We know how cash will behave generally. So I think, you know, that's a really valuable asset that people don't think about in portfolios.
episode_title: The case for gold, cash ... and caution

headline: Evergreen Consultants building exposure to gold and critical minerals as portfolio hedges in uncertain macro environment
reasoning: Angela Ashton notes that Evergreen has been allocating incrementally more to gold and critical minerals as alternative, uncorrelated assets. These are viewed as hedges within the portfolio, particularly in the context of a stagflation-light environment where traditional asset classes may struggle. The allocation is framed as part of a broader alternatives-building strategy.
quote: We've also been allocating a little bit more to things like gold, um, critical minerals broadly, um, as well. They're the sorts of things, I guess, that we're thinking of as being alternatives.
episode_title: The case for gold, cash ... and caution

headline: Evergreen Consultants keeping duration very low across both Australian and global fixed interest exposures
reasoning: Angela Ashton notes that Evergreen has kept duration very low across both domestic and global fixed interest allocations. Instead of holding traditional bonds, they have substituted into very high quality credit to eke out some yield while building cash weightings. This reflects their view that a higher-for-longer inflation environment is unfavourable for duration risk.
quote: We've kept duration very low. So our fixed interest exposures both globally and Australian are very low. Um, but what we've done is we've, we've used very high quality credit instead to try and, and, you know, sort of eke out some yield while increasing cash weightings while we can.
episode_title: The case for gold, cash ... and caution

headline: Evergreen Consultants cautious on hedge funds despite appeal of the concept, citing high cost, low liquidity, and poor crisis performance
reasoning: Angela Ashton acknowledges the conceptual appeal of hedge funds as alternatives but is wary of them in practice. She notes they tend to be expensive, carry low liquidity, and often fail to deliver when most needed because correlations converge to one during crises — even the best hedge funds have shown they cannot fully withstand severe market dislocations.
quote: Hedge funds. We're starting to look at a little bit. But the reality is a lot of them are pretty expensive, have low liquidity, and often don't deliver what you really need them to when things really fall apart. So correlations, you know, sort of all go to one when there's a crisis. And even the best hedge funds sort of, you know, have shown us that they don't withstand those sorts of situations. So we're a bit wary of hedge funds, although the idea is great.
episode_title: The case for gold, cash ... and caution

headline: Evergreen Consultants sees Australia in a 'stagflation light' environment with inflation remaining higher for longer than markets expect
reasoning: Angela Ashton describes the current environment as 'stagflation light' — not as severe as the 1970s and 80s, but inflation is running structurally higher than the 2010-2020 decade. She believes inflationary expectations are becoming entrenched and that investors are underestimating how long it takes for inflation to unwind. She warns this environment is generally unfavourable for many asset classes and that investors need to think about inflation's impact on portfolios much more carefully.
quote: I would call it at the moment what's looking like a stagflation light environment. It's certainly not stagflation in the way that we had in the 70s and 80s and all that sort of thing. But certainly it's a stagflation light environment, and that's often not good for a lot of different types of assets. So we're thinking about what, um, you know, we're thinking about inflation a lot more in portfolios and how that can affect portfolios broadly. So that's, you know, something that I think people need to really think about a lot more because it's endemic. Um, you know, inflationary expectations are sort of starting to become quite set. And I think people are underestimating that. They often do. They think inflation comes and goes and and it doesn't. It takes a long time to wind out.
episode_title: The case for gold, cash ... and caution

headline: Resources sector delivered standout earnings in Australian reporting season, broadly in line with analyst expectations set earlier in the year
